info.name: SmartKey API
info.description: Every server-side route in SmartKey (78 requests covering 69 unique method + path combinations across 63 route files), grouped by the role that calls it. ## Read this before your first request **1. Auth is cookie-based, not Bearer.** `POST /api/auth/login` writes a Supabase session into a role-namespaced cookie (`sb--cso`, `-dean`, `-verifier`, `-requester`). Postman's cookie jar stores it automatically. Do not set an `Authorization` header on user routes; it is ignored. **2. Every authenticated request MUST send a `Referer` header.** This is the non-obvious part. For `/api/*` paths the middleware cannot derive the role namespace from the URL, so it falls back to the `Referer` (see `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts` and `namespaceFromReferer` in `src/lib/supabase/cookies.ts`). With no `Referer`, the request resolves to the transient `activate` namespace, finds no session, and returns 401 — even though you are logged in. Every request in this collection already carries the correct `Referer`. If you copy a request elsewhere, carry the header with it: | Calling role | Referer value | | --- | --- | | CSO | `{{baseUrl}}/cso` | | Dean | `{{baseUrl}}/dean` | | Verifier | `{{baseUrl}}/verifier` | | Requester | `{{baseUrl}}/requester` | The `x-smartkey-namespace` header is set by the middleware and overwritten on every request, so sending it yourself does nothing. **3. CSO, Dean and Verifier require email OTP.** Login returns `mfa_required: true` and mails a 6-digit code; the session is not usable until `POST /api/auth/verify-otp` succeeds. Requester skips MFA and is signed in straight from login. **4. Response envelope.** Every route returns `{ data, error, status }`. On success `error` is null; on failure `data` is null and `error` is a user-facing string. 204 responses have no body. See `docs/postman/README.md` for the full walkthrough and `docs/API.md` for the per-route reference.

Auto-filled where possible; otherwise paste a keys.id UUID.
6-digit collection code; auto-filled on submit / weekend-code.

item.name: 00 — Auth
item.description: Start here. Run Login, then Verify OTP for CSO/Dean/Verifier. Postman stores the session cookie for you.

exec: console.warn('Sign-in OK, but the OTP email could not be sent (SMTP unreachable?).');
console.warn('Run "Resend OTP" — the stored code is still valid.');
console.log('MFA required — check the inbox, set {{otp}}, then run Verify OTP.');
console.log('Signed in without MFA as', body.data.role);

request.description: Verifies credentials on a throwaway client, then writes the session into the cookie namespace for the account's role. Returns `{ session, role, mfa_required, email_delivery_failed }`. For CSO / DEAN / VERIFIER `mfa_required` is true, `session` is null, and a 6-digit code is emailed — the session cookie exists but is only usable after Verify OTP. REQUESTER returns a live session and `mfa_required: false`. **`email_delivery_failed`** (MFA roles only) is true when the credentials were accepted but the code email could not be sent — e.g. SMTP blocked on your network, which is common locally on port 587. This is **not** a login failure: the code hash is already stored, so run **Resend OTP** and the code it delivers is valid. Before 2026-08-02 this path returned a 500 and made the whole collection unusable when SMTP was unreachable. No `Referer` needed: this route passes the namespace explicitly. Errors: 401 invalid credentials · 422 schema · 503 auth service unreachable (distinguished from 401 via `isAuthRetryableFetchError`, so a network blip never reads as a wrong password).
Same route as above. REQUESTER is the only role exempt from MFA, so this single call leaves you fully signed in — the fastest path to exercising the requester flow.

Completes MFA. `email` is required alongside `otp` — the route looks the profile up by `institutional_email` to know which cookie namespace login wrote to. The stored code is a SHA-256 hash with a 10-minute expiry and is cleared on success, so a code cannot be replayed. Writes a `LOGIN_SUCCEEDED` audit entry with `method: 'OTP'`. Errors: 401 invalid or expired code · 422 schema.
Mints a fresh 10-minute MFA code. Always returns 200 with `data: null` whether or not the email matches a profile — deliberate, to prevent account enumeration.

header.description: Required — selects the session cookie namespace.

request.description: Re-authenticates with `current_password` before applying the change, so a hijacked session alone cannot rotate the password. Writes a `PASSWORD_CHANGED` audit entry. `new_password` must satisfy `src/lib/validation/primitives.ts`: 12–64 chars with upper, lower, digit and symbol. Errors: 401 not authenticated or wrong current password · 422 policy failure.
Triggers the Supabase password-reset email. Always 200 (no enumeration). The emailed link lands on `GET /api/auth/callback`.
Invalidates the current Supabase session. No body. The `Referer` decides which role's session is ended — omit it and you will clear the wrong namespace.

formdata.description: 12–64 chars, upper + lower + digit + symbol.

request.description: Multipart. **Not directly runnable in Postman** without first completing the invite link in a browser: there is no `token` field — the invite is a Supabase magic link that resolves through `GET /api/auth/callback` into a session in the `activate` namespace, and this route only reads that session. Listed here so the contract is documented. Errors: 401 no activation session · 422 weak password or missing photo · 413 photo over 5 MB.

response.name: Error

request.description: One-time Dean onboarding. Same activation-session precondition as Register — no `token` field. Stores the two images in the `hod-signatures` bucket and writes their URLs to `profiles.signature_ref_url` / `stamp_ref_url`. The signature becomes the reference every later weekend approval is pixel-matched against. Errors: 401 no activation session · 403 profile is not DEAN · 422 validation · 413 image over 5 MB.

query.description: The hashed_token from admin.generateLink() — not runnable standalone from Postman since it requires a real link minted server-side by provision_user / resend-invite / reset-password.
verification_type from generateLink: invite, recovery, etc. type=recovery gets its own failure redirect.
Where to send the user after the session is established. Defaults to /.

request.description: Not a JSON API — a redirect handler, and the actual session-establishment mechanism for every emailed one-time link the app generates (invite, re-invite, password reset). Calls verifyOtp({type, token_hash}) server-side — no PKCE code_verifier involved, which matters because the link is minted by the admin API, not by a browser that could have stored one. Session lands in the transient activate namespace, then redirects to next. On failure: type=recovery redirects to /reset-password?error=expired; everything else redirects to /login?error=invalid-link. Not directly runnable from Postman with a fabricated token_hash — included so the invite/activation flow reads end to end. See docs/API.md.

query.description: One-time PKCE code from the emailed link.
Where to send the user afterwards. Defaults to /.

request.description: Not a JSON API — a redirect handler for the PKCE ?code=... shape (exchangeCodeForSession). Not used by any in-app flow — invite, re-invite, and password reset all route through GET /auth/confirm instead (see the "Confirm link" request below), because exchangeCodeForSession needs a code_verifier cookie that only exists in a browser that itself started the flow, which is never true for an admin-generated link. Retained only as a dead-but-harmless fallback in case a Supabase-configured redirect ever points here.

item.name: 01 — Requester
item.description: Sign in with 'Login (Requester)' first. No OTP step for this role.

request.description: Calls the `create_request` RPC, which checks authorisation, runs the rule-based risk engine, mints the code and writes the audit entry in one transaction. WEEKDAY returns a 6-digit code immediately (`CODE_ISSUED`, 10-minute expiry). WEEKEND returns **no code** and lands on `PENDING_HOD` awaiting a Dean/CSO decision — the code is minted on the day via 'Get weekend code'. Optional `letter_url` attaches a Dean-signed letter (uploaded client-side to `weekend-letters`) so signature verification can run at approval. Errors: 403 not authorised for this key · 409 an active request already exists for it · 422 outside operational hours.

response.name: Error

request.description: `weekend_date` must be a Saturday or Sunday. Response is `{ request_id, status: 'PENDING_HOD', risk_tier }` — deliberately no code. Next stop: the Dean's queue.

response.name: Error

request.description: Cursor-paginated history for the signed-in requester, newest first, with the key joined. Returns `{ requests, next_cursor }`.

Mints the 10-minute collection code for an `APPROVED` weekend request — **only on the requested date**. Moves it to `CODE_ISSUED`. The code is deliberately never emailed at approval time; keeping it short-lived and same-day is the whole point of the weekend flow. Errors: 403 not your request · 409 not in APPROVED state · 422 TOO_EARLY (before the date).

response.name: Error

request.description: Generates a 6-digit **return** code (15-minute expiry) the requester reads out at the desk, so a verifier cannot log a phantom return alone. Status stays `KEY_ISSUED`; audit `RETURN_CODE_GENERATED`. Errors: 403 not your request · 409 key not currently issued · 404 not found.

Fired automatically by the UI when the countdown hits 0. Idempotent — returns the current status without erroring if the request already moved on. Note the branch: a WEEKEND code lapsing **on its own date** rolls back to `APPROVED` (audit `CODE_EXPIRED`) so the requester can mint a fresh one the same day. A weekday code, or a weekend code after the date has passed, terminates to `EXPIRED`. Errors: 403 not your request · 409 code has not expired yet.

Cancellable from any pre-collection state you own: `CODE_ISSUED`, or `PENDING_HOD` / `APPROVED` for a weekend request whose code has not been minted — the manual escape hatch before the nightly job expires it. Errors: 403 not your request · 409 not in a cancellable state.

response.name: Error

item.name: 02 — Dean
item.description: Sign in as a Dean (login + verify OTP). Scoped to the Dean's own unit by RLS.

request.description: `status = 'PENDING_HOD'` for the Dean's unit, including external (guest) requests with the guest details, `letter_url` and `requested_unit_id` joined so the Dean can review and assign a key before approving. Also callable by the **CSO**, who gets the Administration-routed requests (units with `authoriser = 'CSO'` have no Dean).

Moves the request to `APPROVED` via the `approve_weekend` RPC. **No code is minted here** — the requester mints one on the day. So the success status is `"APPROVED"`, never `"CODE_ISSUED"`. If you include `submitted_signature_url`, the letter's signature is pixel-matched (Sharp + Pixelmatch) against the Dean's onboarded reference first. Over the threshold (default 15%) the approval is **held**: the RPC is never called, a `SIGNATURE_MISMATCH` audit entry is written, and you get HTTP **200** with `{ status: 'HELD_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH', mismatch_pct }` — a held approval is not a route error, so check the status field, not just the HTTP code. The RPC re-validates the actor against the unit's `authoriser`, so a Dean acting on an Administration key (or the CSO on a faculty key) is rejected with 403 regardless of what the route allowed.

response.name: Error

request.description: Same endpoint, guest branch. When the request has a `guest_id`, `key_id` becomes **required** — a guest picks a unit, not a key, so the Dean assigns the actual key at approval. Routes to `approve_guest_weekend`. Signature verification is skipped: guests have no reference signature on file, so the Dean reviews the uploaded letter by eye (see 'Preview authorisation letter').

response.name: Error

request.description: Routes to `decline_weekend`. Returns `{ status: 'DECLINED' }`. Works for guest and registered requests alike; no `key_id` needed.

response.name: Error

request.description: Returns a 5-minute signed URL for the guest's uploaded letter. The `weekend-letters` bucket is private; signing happens server-side with the admin client and is gated to the Dean whose unit owns the request (CSO also permitted). Errors: 403 not your unit · 404 request has no letter.

response.name: Error

request.description: Shared with the CSO. A Dean automatically sees only their own unit's keys (enforced in-query and by RLS); the CSO sees everything. Backs the Dean dashboard's recent-activity feed.

header.description: Required. Resolves the role cookie namespace for /api/* paths — without it the request 401s even when signed in.

request.description: Clears a weekend request whose `requested_for` date has passed out of the pending queue. A lapsed request can no longer be approved or declined — both RPCs refuse a past date — so without this it sits in the Dean's (or CSO's) list until the nightly `expire_stale_weekend_requests()` sweep at 00:15 UTC. This is housekeeping, not a decision on merits: no `hod_decisions` row is written. The request moves to `EXPIRED`, the same terminal state the cron produces, so it stays visible in requester history and the CSO audit log. The `REQUEST_EXPIRED` audit payload carries `reason: 'dismissed_by_authoriser'`, the previous status, and the dismissing actor. **Roles**: Dean (own faculty only) · CSO (any, including Administration). Swap the `Referer` to `{{baseUrl}}/cso` when calling as CSO. **Errors**: `403` not a Dean/CSO, or the request is not in your faculty · `404` not found · `409` the request is still live (approve or decline it instead) or is already terminal · `422` validation.

item.name: 03 — Verifier
item.description: The security desk. Sign in as a Verifier (login + verify OTP), then start a shift.

request.description: No body. Opens a shift for the signed-in officer and derives the next shift number (wraps 1→2→3→1). Rejects with 409 if a shift is already open — the officer should run the handover instead. Returns 201.

response.name: Error

request.description: The open shift with officer identities and elapsed time. Also readable by the CSO.
All `CODE_ISSUED` requests, oldest first. This is the **initial load only** — the dashboard keeps itself current over a Supabase Realtime subscription, so do not poll this.

The desk's highest-frequency call. `code` is the only field — the verifier is taken from the server-verified session, and any client-supplied `verifier_id` is deliberately ignored so a collection cannot be attributed to another officer. The response carries `is_guest`. For a guest it is true and `requester` holds the declared ID document with a null `photo_url` (the officer checks the physical ID); for a registered requester you get the passport photo. The shape is additive, so registered-only consumers are unaffected. Errors: 404 code not found or expired · 409 key already issued.

Everything currently out. Shared with the CSO. Overdue is **derived**, not just read: the hourly `mark_key_overdue` job flips the key's own status, but the route also compares `return_deadline` to now, so the badge is correct even between cron runs. Rows come back with `status: 'KEY_OVERDUE'` in that case.

Exactly one of `code` or `override_reason` must be present — the schema refuses both-missing. This is the verified path: the requester read out their return code, so the audit event is `KEY_RETURNED`. Add `returner_id` if someone other than the original requester is handing the key back.

response.name: Error

request.description: The escape hatch when the requester cannot produce a code. Completes the return but records it as `KEY_RETURNED_UNVERIFIED` **and** raises a `SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY` incident to the CSO when a shift is open — deliberately visible, never silent. `override_reason` must be at least 3 characters.

response.name: Error

request.description: The incoming officer acknowledges every outstanding key. `key_ids` must match the actual outstanding set or you get 422 — this is chain-of-custody, so a partial list is rejected rather than quietly accepted. One audit entry is written per key. Errors: 409 handover already completed for this shift.

response.name: Error

request.description: Append-only — there is no update or delete endpoint by design, mirroring a physical incident book. `type`: MISSING_KEY | SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY | EQUIPMENT_FAULT | PROCEDURAL | OTHER. `severity`: LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH. Optional `related_key_id`, `related_person_id`. HIGH severity additionally raises a realtime CSO alert. Returns a human-readable `reference` like `INC-2026-0042`.

item.name: 04 — CSO · oversight
item.description: Monitoring, incidents, reports and AI alert surfaces. Sign in as CSO (login + verify OTP).

request.description: Requests with `risk_tier = 'HIGH'` and status `CODE_ISSUED` or `KEY_ISSUED`. Worth being precise about: there is **no `PENDING_CSO` status** in the schema. High risk does not hold a request for CSO sign-off — this is a review/intervention surface over requests that are already issuable or issued, not a gate in front of the Dean decision.

item.name: CSO decision on a high-risk request

request.description: Intervention, not an approval gate. `DECLINED` cancels the request (`CODE_ISSUED` → `CANCELLED`, audit `REQUEST_DECLINED_CSO`). `APPROVED` changes no state at all — it is a recorded acknowledgement that the CSO reviewed it and let it stand (audit `REQUEST_APPROVED_CSO`). `note` is accepted by the schema but is not currently persisted anywhere.
Unresolved HIGH-tier requests from the last 24 hours. Read-only — the rule engine runs at submit time, not here, so this never recomputes a score.

Weekend requests stuck on `PENDING_HOD` with an unresolved `SIGNATURE_MISMATCH` audit entry. Each alert carries both image URLs and the mismatch percentage so the CSO can compare side by side. A request drops off this list once resolved via `cso_override` on hod-decision (next request).

Lets the CSO settle a faculty-key request that a Dean's approval attempt held on a signature mismatch. This is **not** a general bypass of the Dean-authoriser gate: the RPC itself checks that a `SIGNATURE_MISMATCH` audit entry already exists for the request and returns 403 otherwise. Enforced in the function body, not just the route, so it holds even if something calls the RPC directly.

response.name: Error

request.description: Read-only, cursor-paginated. Append-only log — no update or delete endpoint exists.
Retires the key and opens a `MISSING_KEY` incident at HIGH severity in one go. Returns `{ key_id, incident_id }`. Writes an audit entry.
Cursor-paginated list of generated reports.

Creates the immutable `shift_reports` row via RPC (uniqueness guard + audit entry), then calls Gemini with the shift's audit events and persists `{ markdown, timeline, metadata }` through the admin client — RLS blocks a direct UPDATE even for the CSO. Falls back to a deterministic template when Gemini is unavailable or the output will not parse, so generation always succeeds. Every report renders with a 'Generated by AI from shift event data' disclosure. Errors: 409 a report already exists for this shift.

response.name: Error

request.description: The report body itself is immutable; comments are the sanctioned way to annotate it. Comments are themselves immutable after insert.
Same route the Dean calls, but unscoped — the CSO sees every unit.

item.name: 05 — CSO · administration
item.description: User provisioning, units, key inventory and collector authorisation slots.

request.description: Returns **every** non-deactivated profile in one shot with the unit joined. Deliberately takes no query params and does no pagination — filtering and paging happen client-side in the CSO users table. Do not expect `next_cursor` here.

Creates the profile, mints a 24-hour activation token, queues the invite email and writes the audit entry — all inside the `provision_user` RPC. `role` is DEAN | VERIFIER | REQUESTER (never CSO — that account is seeded). `unit_id` is required for DEAN and REQUESTER. Note the RPC parameter is still named `p_department_id` for historical reasons but writes to `profiles.unit_id`. Errors: 409 email already registered · 422 validation.

Name and unit only. Email and role are intentionally **not** editable: the email is the auth login identity and the chain-of-trust anchor, and role changes are out of scope. Moving a Dean keeps the `units.hod_id` reverse link in sync. The `USER_UPDATED` audit entry records only fields that actually changed. Errors: 409 destination unit already has a Dean · 422 unit required / not found.

response.name: Error

request.description: No body. Sets `status = 'DEACTIVATED'` and invalidates the Supabase session immediately. The profile row is kept so the audit trail stays intact — accounts are never deleted. Errors: 404 not found · 409 already deactivated.

No body. Sends a fresh activation link to a user still `PENDING_ACTIVATION` — for when the original 24-hour link lapsed unused. Errors: 409 user is already ACTIVE, or is DEACTIVATED (reinstate first).

Every unit — a faculty, or the single Administration group. Each row carries its Dean, a `hasActiveHod` flag (used to grey the unit out in the Dean-role picker) and `hasAvailableKey`. Run this first: it populates `{{unitId}}` for the provisioning calls.

Adds a key to the inventory at status `AVAILABLE`. Returns 201 with `{ key_id }`. `code` must match `^[A-Z0-9]+-\d+$` (e.g. `NS-304`). `key_count` (1–20, default 1) is how many physical keys are on the bunch — the verifier sees it at issue and return.

Fills one of the three collector slots for a key. Called by the **Dean** for their own unit's keys, or the **CSO** for Administration keys — the route delegates entirely to the authoriser-aware `nominate_collector` RPC, which is why one endpoint serves both roles. Switch the `Referer` to `{{baseUrl}}/dean` when testing as a Dean. The max-3 limit is a database trigger, not an application check, so it cannot be raced past. Errors: 403 key outside your scope · 409 three slots already filled · 409 already authorised.

response.name: Error

request.description: Frees a slot. Same authoriser-aware rules as nomination. Returns **204 with no body** — `apiFetch` normalises that to `{ data: null, error: null, status: 204 }`. Errors: 403 key outside your scope · 404 authorisation not found.

header.description: Required. Resolves the role cookie namespace for /api/* paths — without it the request 401s even when signed in.

request.description: Returns the live risk-engine configuration that backs the `/cso/settings` "Risk rules" screen: one row per rule (`rule_key`, `weight`, `enabled`) plus the singleton tier boundaries (`medium_min`, `high_min`). The engine reads this at request-submit time, so changes take effect on the next request without a deploy. If the read fails, `POST /api/requests/submit` falls back to the hardcoded `DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG` rather than failing the key request. **Roles**: CSO only.

header.description: Required. Resolves the role cookie namespace for /api/* paths — without it the request 401s even when signed in.

request.description: Replaces the whole risk configuration in one call. Writes go through the `update_risk_config` RPC — the tables have no write policy for any role — and produce a single `RISK_CONFIG_UPDATED` audit entry per save, not one per rule. **The `rules` array must contain all five rule keys exactly once.** Partial updates are rejected. `weight` is an integer 1–10 (enforced by a `CHECK` constraint, not just Zod). `high_min` must exceed `medium_min`, likewise enforced at the DB level. Disabled rules are skipped entirely by the engine — they never appear in a request’s `risk_factors`. **Roles**: CSO only. **Errors**: `403` not CSO · `422` missing/duplicate rule key, weight out of range, or `high_min <= medium_min`.

header.description: Required. Resolves the role cookie namespace for /api/* paths — without it the request 401s even when signed in.

request.description: Returns the live operational settings backing the `/cso/settings` "Operational" screen: per-zone weekday/weekend hours (`zone_hours`) and the singleton `return_deadline_time` / `code_expiry_minutes` (`operational_config`), all times as `HH:MM`. **Roles**: CSO only.

header.description: Required. Resolves the role cookie namespace for /api/* paths — without it the request 401s even when signed in.

request.description: Replaces zone hours and the return-deadline/code-expiry singleton in one call, via the `update_operational_config` RPC (no table has a direct write policy). One save writes one `OPERATIONAL_CONFIG_UPDATED` audit entry. Takes effect on the next request submission or code-generation call — requests already in progress keep their original deadline/expiry. **`zones` must contain exactly one entry per zone value.** Weekend hours are required unless `weekend_closed` is true. Only the collection-code expiry (`code_expiry_minutes`) is affected here — the separate 15-minute return-code expiry is untouched. **Roles**: CSO only. **Errors**: `403` not CSO · `422` bad `HH:MM` value, missing weekend hours while not closed, or `code_expiry_minutes` outside 5–60.

item.name: 06 — Profile (any signed-in role)
item.description: Self-service account settings. Change the Referer to match whichever role you are signed in as.

request.description: The caller's own profile including role-specific fields (`signature_ref_url` / `stamp_ref_url` for Deans) and the joined unit. Backs every role's settings page.
Only `full_name` is mutable here. Email belongs to Supabase Auth, the photo has its own route, and unit/role changes are CSO-only via `/api/admin/users/[id]`.

Multipart. Replaces the caller's own photo in the `passport-photos` bucket — the storage path is keyed by user id, so one route serves every role. Errors: 422 missing file or non-image · 413 over 5 MB.

response.name: Error

request.description: Removes the stored file(s) and clears `photo_url`. No body.

Dean-only, post-onboarding replacement. If a reference already exists the upload is pixel-matched against it first — you cannot silently swap the specimen every later approval is checked against. Over threshold: the reference is **not** replaced, a `SIGNATURE_MISMATCH` audit entry (`context: 'reference_replacement'`) goes to the CSO, and you get HTTP 200 with `{ status: 'HELD_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH', mismatch_pct, message }`. Under threshold: `{ status: 'updated', new_url }` plus a `SIGNATURE_REFERENCE_UPDATED` entry. Errors: 403 not DEAN · 422 bad type or missing image · 413 over 5 MB.

response.name: Error

header.description: Required. Resolves the role cookie namespace for /api/* paths — without it the request 401s even when signed in.

request.description: The caller's own `notification_preferences` row (RLS-scoped, no role check — the table is role-agnostic and each role's settings screen only reads/writes the columns it displays). Returns defaults (all `true` except `digest_email`) when no row exists yet; a row is only created on first save. Swap the `Referer` for the calling role: `/cso`, `/dean`, or `/requester`.

response.name: Success

header.description: Required. Resolves the role cookie namespace for /api/* paths — without it the request 401s even when signed in.

request.description: Upserts the caller's own row. All fields are individually optional but at least one is required; Postgrest only touches the columns present in the body, so one role's PATCH never disturbs another role's columns on the same row shape. No RPC, no audit entry — same trust level as `PATCH /api/profile/me`. There is no `code_email` field — the collection-code email can't be disabled. **Roles**: ALL (authenticated). **Errors**: `401` unauthenticated · `422` empty body.

item.name: 07 — Public · guest weekend access
item.description: No authentication anywhere in this folder. An external person with no SmartKey account requests weekend access; a Dean approves and assigns a key; the guest mints a code on the day. Identified end to end by an unguessable access_token. Also in this folder: the one-click Dean decision link from the "New weekend request" email (decision_token), which covers both guest and registered-requester weekend requests routed to a Dean-authorised unit — not guest-only, but unauthenticated in the same way.

formdata.description: Free text — the guest states what they need; the Dean assigns the actual key.
Field name is still department_id even though the table is now units.
ISO date, must be Sat or Sun.
Dean authorisation letter. PDF, JPG or PNG, max 5 MB.

request.description: Multipart, unauthenticated, returns 201. Guests are modelled as their own `guest_requesters` entity — never a profile, because `profiles.id` references `auth.users` and a guest profile would require an auth user and break the `invited_by` chain of trust. Uploads the letter to the private `weekend-letters` bucket, creates the request at `PENDING_HOD` with no code, and emails the status link. A failed email is logged but does not fail the request — hence the `access_token` in the response as a fallback. The whole `/api/public/*` prefix bypasses session resolution in middleware, and the underlying guest RPCs have execute revoked from `anon`/`public` — they run only through this server route with the service-role client. Errors: 404 unit not found · 422 validation · 413 letter over 5 MB.

The session-less status page payload, read by `access_token`. Returns only safe fields: status, requested date, the room they asked for, the assigned key once a Dean has picked one, and the code + expiry while `CODE_ISSUED`. `key` is null until approval; `code` / `code_expires_at` are non-null only while `CODE_ISSUED`.

response.name: Success

request.description: Guest analogue of the requester's weekend-code call. 10-minute code, on the requested date only, moving the request to `CODE_ISSUED`. No body. Errors: 409 not in APPROVED state · 422 TOO_EARLY · 404 token not found.

response.name: Error

request.description: Guest analogue of `POST /api/requests/request-return` — a 15-minute return code so the guest is in the loop on the handback just like a registered requester. No body; status stays `KEY_ISSUED`. The verifier then enters it through the normal `POST /api/keys/return`, which validates a return code regardless of whether the holder is registered or a guest. Errors: 404 token not found · 409 key not currently issued.
Fired by the guest status page when the countdown hits 0. Idempotent. Same same-day rollback semantics as the registered path. Errors: 409 code has not expired yet · 404 token not found.

Read-only. Looks up the request by `decision_token` and returns what the confirmation page needs: requester/guest details, key or requested room, short-lived signed letter/stamp URLs, and — for a still-`PENDING_HOD` guest request — `available_keys` for the key picker. Never mutates state (mail-scanner safety: Outlook/Gmail prefetch links, so a GET that decided anything would let a scanner silently approve or decline before a human opens the email). `decidable` is `status === 'PENDING_HOD'` — the page renders Approve/Decline only when true. **Roles**: ALL (unauthenticated). **Errors**: `404` token not found or malformed.

request.description: Re-resolves the unit's **current** Dean at decision time (handles a Dean handover between the email being sent and acted on), then runs the same `decideWeekendRequest` core as `POST /api/requests/hod-decision` — verification, mismatch-holding, guest key-assignment, and the requester notification all behave identically to the dashboard flow. For a guest request, `key_id` is required when `decision` is `APPROVED` (pick one from the prior GET's `available_keys`). Registered-requester approvals read `letter_url`/`stamp_url` off the request row itself as the submitted signature/stamp. **Roles**: ALL (unauthenticated). **Errors**: `403` unit no longer Dean-authorised, or has no Dean · `404` token not found, or resolves to no unit · `409` request no longer `PENDING_HOD` · `422` validation, or (guest `APPROVED`) missing `key_id`.

response.name: Error — already decided

item.name: 08 — System (secret-guarded)
item.description: Not user-facing and not called from a browser. Both routes authenticate with a shared secret rather than a session. Populate {{cronSecret}} / {{serviceRoleKey}} from .env.local before running.

header.description: Shared CRON_SECRET — not a user session.

request.description: Called by the `weekend-code-reminders` pg_cron job at 06:00 UTC on Sat/Sun. Emails every `APPROVED` weekend request due today (registered and guest) a nudge to mint their code, then stamps `reminder_sent_at` so a retry never double-sends. No collection code is ever included — the code is always minted on the day. pg_cron reads the bearer secret from Supabase Vault (`weekend_cron_secret`), which must match `CRON_SECRET`. Returns `{ sent, failed }`. Errors: 401 wrong/missing secret · 500 CRON_SECRET not configured.

header.description: Shared CRON_SECRET — not a user session.

request.description: Called by the `overdue-key-check` pg_cron job hourly, right after `mark_key_overdue()` in the same job. Emails every requester (registered and guest) whose `KEY_ISSUED` request has passed its `return_deadline`, skipping registered requesters who opted out via `notification_preferences.overdue_email` (default true; guests have no preference and always receive it). Stamps `overdue_reminder_sent_at` on every processed row, including ones suppressed by preference, so a row is never re-queried every hour. Returns `{ sent, suppressed, failed }`. Errors: 401 wrong/missing secret · 500 CRON_SECRET not configured.

header.description: Shared CRON_SECRET — not a user session.

request.description: Called by the `daily-digest` pg_cron job at 07:00 UTC. For every `ACTIVE` Dean/CSO profile with `notification_preferences.digest_email = true` (absence of a row means **not** opted in — the opposite default from every other preference column), calls the `get_digest_stats` RPC for the last 24 hours (building-wide for a CSO, per-unit for a Dean) and emails a summary. Skips a recipient whose window has nothing to report in any relevant field. Returns `{ sent, skipped, failed }`. Errors: 401 wrong/missing secret · 500 CRON_SECRET not configured.

header.description: Shared CRON_SECRET — not a user session.

request.description: Called by the `audit-log-export` pg_cron job at 02:00 UTC. Exports fully-completed UTC calendar days of `audit_log` to Vercel Blob (`access: 'private'`) as newline-delimited JSON (`audit-log/YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson`), advancing the `audit_export_state` watermark one day at a time so a mid-run failure only loses progress on the day that failed. `audit_log` itself is never mutated — RLS denies UPDATE/DELETE for every role, this is additive durability, not a retention policy. Capped at 20,000 rows per invocation. Returns `{ exported_days, exported_rows }`. Errors: 401 wrong/missing secret · 500 CRON_SECRET / BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN not configured, or upload failure.

Exposes the Sharp + Pixelmatch pipeline directly: fetches the Dean's reference and the submitted image, greyscales both, normalises to 800×400, thresholds to binary, then diffs pixel by pixel. Returns `{ mismatch_ratio, passed }` against `SIGNATURE_DIFF_THRESHOLD` (default 0.55, scored over the ink region only — see docs/AI.md). Useful for calibrating the threshold against real signature samples. Errors: 403 wrong internal secret · 422 Dean has no reference signature on file.

item.name: 09 — Ops (uptime monitoring)
item.description: No authentication, no cookies, no session. A liveness probe for external uptime monitoring (e.g. UptimeRobot) — the one thing the statically-rendered landing page can't do, which is fail when the database is unreachable.

request.description: Issues a real (RLS-denied, zero-row) query against `keys` using the anon client, proving PostgREST and Postgres are both reachable. Never uses the service role — this route is public and unauthenticated by design. Reports `degraded` (still HTTP 200) when the round trip exceeds 1000ms, `ok` otherwise. **Roles**: none (public). **Errors**: `503` database unreachable, or the Supabase client failed to construct (e.g. missing env vars).
